title: Projective model structures on complex-enriched diagrams and cofibrant evaluation
statement:
Use the dg-category, cochain-complex and model-category conventions of [lem-coef-dgcat-model-structure], in sufficiently large universes. Let $\mathcal N$ be a complete and cocomplete locally presentable category enriched, tensored and cotensored over $\mathrm{Ch}(\mathbf Z)$. Here enrichment means unital associative composition chain maps on complexes $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(X,Y)$ whose degree-zero cycles are the ordinary morphisms. Tensors $K\otimes X$ and cotensors $Y^K$ satisfy the natural complex adjunctions $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(K\otimes X,Y)\cong\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathrm{Ch}}(K,\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(X,Y))\cong\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(X,Y^K)$. Locally presentable means that, for some regular cardinal $\kappa$, a set of objects whose ordinary Hom functors preserve $\kappa$-filtered colimits generates all objects under $\kappa$-filtered colimits. Suppose it has a cofibrantly generated model structure and satisfies the enriched model axiom: for a cofibration $i:P\to Q$ and a fibration $p:X\to Y$, the map
$$\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(Q,X)\longrightarrow\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P,X)\times_{\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P,Y)}\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(Q,Y)$$
is a degreewise surjection of complexes, and is a quasi-isomorphism if $i$ or $p$ is a weak equivalence. An object is cofibrant if its initial map is a cofibration, and fibrant if its terminal map is a fibration. Assume a set $I$ of generating cofibrations has cofibrant domains and codomains, and write $J$ for a set of generating trivial cofibrations. Generating means that the maps having the right lifting property against $I$, respectively $J$, are precisely the trivial fibrations, respectively fibrations. For every small dg category $\mathcal C$ over $\mathbf Z$, the category $\mathcal N^{\mathcal C}$ of strict complex-enriched functors and enriched natural transformations has the projective cofibrantly generated model structure: weak equivalences and fibrations are detected at each object of $\mathcal C$, and cofibrations have the left lifting property against the objectwise trivial fibrations. It is again complete, cocomplete and locally presentable, enriched, tensored and cotensored over complexes, and satisfies the displayed enriched model axiom for its actual complexes of enriched natural transformations. For functors $F,G$, degree $r$ of this complex consists of families $\eta_c\in\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(F(c),G(c))^r$ satisfying $G(a)\eta_c=(-1)^{r|a|}\eta_{c'}F(a)$ for every homogeneous $a\in\mathcal C(c,c')$; the differential and composition are componentwise. The generating maps are $\mathcal C(c,-)\otimes i$ for $c\in\mathcal C$ and $i\in I$, and $\mathcal C(c,-)\otimes j$ for $j\in J$; the former have cofibrant domains and codomains in $\mathcal N^{\mathcal C}$. If every object of $\mathcal N$ is fibrant, the same is true in $\mathcal N^{\mathcal C}$.

If every $\mathcal C(c,c')$ is cofibrant in the projective model structure on complexes, evaluation at every $c$ preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations, hence sends cofibrant diagrams to cofibrant objects. Here $\mathcal C(c,-)\otimes P$ is the enriched free diagram whose value at $c'$ is $\mathcal C(c,c')\otimes P$, left adjoint to evaluation at $c$.

The category $\mathcal N=\mathrm{Ch}(\mathbf Z)$ with weak equivalences the quasi-isomorphisms, fibrations the degreewise surjections and cofibrations defined by lifting satisfies all the hypotheses above, and all its objects are fibrant. Its generating cofibrations may be taken as $S^{n+1}\to D^n$ and its generating trivial cofibrations as $0\to D^n$, for all $n\in\mathbf Z$, where $S^{n+1}$ is $\mathbf Z$ in degree $n+1$ and zero elsewhere, and $D^n$ is $\mathbf Z\xrightarrow{1}\mathbf Z$ in degrees $n,n+1$; the sphere-to-disk map is the identity in degree $n+1$ and zero in every other degree.
